newsitem.title: USA: Slip in U.S. home sales hints housing is sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Slip in U.S. home sales hints housing is sluggish.

text.p: A larger-than-expected decline in U.S. existing home sales suggests slowing in the housing market and should cheer homebuyers, economists said on Monday.

Existing homes sales dipped to an annual rate of 3.97 million units in October, compared with 4.03 million the month before, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) said. Experts had expected a smaller drop, to about 4.0 million.
"Relatively high interest rates, mortgage rates and a slowing employment environment are what's slowing down the housing market at this time," said Kurt Karl of WEFA Group.
Karl, who is WEFA's chief economist for U.S. forecasting, said although interest rates have come off lately, sluggish jobs growth has added to any weakness in the housing sector.

"It looks like we're in a slowdown phase," said Karl. But he added that "something close to 4.0 million in existing home sales is a big number." A low number would be closer to 3.0 or 3.5 million units, he said.
Another housing measure, new home sales for October, is scheduled to be released next week. After a couple of strong months, it too should have declined, economists said.
"We would expect now a decline in new home sales," said Karl. "It's been surprisingly strong."

The performance of the housing sector often predicts overall economic growth, said Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc. If housing has cooled, economic growth should remain tepid near term, he said.
"It indicates the economy continues to slow and probably points toward continued slow consumer durables spending early next year," said Kretzmer.
"It was a puzzle" that gross domestic product growth dipped in the third and fourth quarters without being led by slower housing, Kretzmer said.
October single-family home sales might spark a guarded rally in the bond market if it follows suit when it is released next Tuesday, economists said.

"Given the other indicators, the market might get a little mileage out of it, but (it) will draw some caution from the idea that housing probably will be supported by the lower mortgage rates we've been seeing," Kretzmer said.
Consumers may have the most to gain from the decline in existing home sales.
"The (housing) market softened and we're having the mortgage rates fall a little lately (so) it's a great time to buy," said Karl.
